original_content.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{1})=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\,$, find $\,T(7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2}).$
original_content.worked_solution:
First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2} & =12{v}_{1}-5{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2} \\  & =12{v}_{1}-5({v}_{1}+{v}_{2}) \\  & =12{v}_{1}-5(0) \\  & =12{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2})=T(12{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(12{v}_{1}) & =12T({v}_{1}) \\  & =12\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 24 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(7{v}_{1}-5{v}_{2})=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 24 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.$

corrected_content.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,\mathbf{T}\,.$ If $\,{\mathbf{v}}_{1}+{\mathbf{v}}_{2}=\mathbf{0}\,$ and $\,\mathbf{T}({\mathbf{v}}_{1})=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\,$, find $\,\mathbf{T}(7{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5{\mathbf{v}}_{2}).$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
First, since ${\mathbf{v}}_{1}+{\mathbf{v}}_{2}=\mathbf{0},$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}7{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5{\mathbf{v}}_{2} & =12{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5{\mathbf{v}}_{2} \\  & =12{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5({\mathbf{v}}_{1}+{\mathbf{v}}_{2}) \\  & =12{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5(\mathbf{0}) \\  & =12{\mathbf{v}}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\mathbf{T}(7{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5{\mathbf{v}}_{2})=\mathbf{T}(12{\mathbf{v}}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $\mathbf{T}$ is a linear transformation, we have that $\mathbf{T}(k\mathbf{v})=k\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{T}(12{\mathbf{v}}_{1}) & =12\mathbf{T}({\mathbf{v}}_{1}) \\  & =12\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 24 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $\mathbf{T}(7{\mathbf{v}}_{1}-5{\mathbf{v}}_{2})=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ 24 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.$
